nodes.label: ncv Architecture Layout
nodes.rationale: Main-window orchestration is isolated in ncv/app.py, shared panel behavior in ncv/ncvcommon.py, and each tab in its own ncv/ncv*.py module so tab implementations stay independently editable.

nodes.label: Offscreen Qt Testing Convention
nodes.rationale: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen lets Qt window creation and .ui form loading be exercised headlessly in CI without a display server.

nodes.label: CF-Style Time Coordinate Decoding
nodes.rationale: Decoding CF time when possible lets datetime coordinates be used directly on plot axes and in limit fields such as `2025-01-01, 2025-12-31`.

nodes.label: Command-Line Interface
nodes.rationale: `ncv [-h] [-m missing_value] [-x] [netcdf_file ...]` takes zero or more files so the app can also start empty and open files from the interface.

nodes.label: Contour Tab
nodes.rationale: A 2D Z slice is drawn as a heat map with one image cell per grid cell rather than interpolated contour lines, keeping the display faithful to the source grid; zlim clips as well as scales the color range.

nodes.label: Dimension Retain/Index/Reduce Selection
nodes.rationale: One uniform selector grammar covers every tab: `all` retains a dimension, a zero-based integer picks an element, and mean/std/min/max/ptp/sum/median/var reduce it, so high-dimensional variables are explicitly narrowed to the dimensionality each view requires.

nodes.label: Limit Field Syntax (xlim/ylim/y2lim/zlim)
nodes.rationale: One shared `min, max` or `(min, max)` grammar across the plotting tabs, where `None` on either bound independently enables automatic scaling for that side only.

nodes.label: Longitude/Latitude Auto-Selection
nodes.rationale: Recognized longitude and latitude variables are chosen automatically as the Map coordinates and as the default Matrix X and Y headers, so the common geospatial case needs no manual wiring.

nodes.label: Map Tab
nodes.rationale: Requires the map/full extra; uses Cartopy only for projection maths and Natural Earth features while pyqtgraph does the drawing. Missing coordinates fall back to a generated regular global lon/lat grid from the data shape.

nodes.label: Matrix and Metadata Tab
nodes.rationale: A read-only array table doubling as the metadata browser: with no Z selected it shows dataset dimensions/variables/groups/attributes, with Z it shows that variable's metadata. It refuses to reshape data implicitly when more than two dimensions remain, asking for more selection instead.

nodes.label: Missing-Data Handling
nodes.rationale: Missing values combine the --miss command-line value, _FillValue, missing_value, and the type's default NetCDF fill value, so metadata-declared sentinels and ad-hoc ones are masked together; NaN and missing render as blank table cells.

nodes.label: netCDF4 Default Reading Backend
nodes.rationale: Supports either one file (groups allowed) or multiple files without groups; group names and multi-file identifiers appear in the variable list.

nodes.label: Optional Install Extras
nodes.rationale: map, xarray, full and test extras sit on a core of netCDF4, NumPy, PyQt6 and pyqtgraph, so the heavy geospatial and dask-adjacent stacks are opt-in and the core install stays small.

nodes.label: pyqtgraph Rendering and Export
nodes.rationale: All plotting tabs rely on pyqtgraph for pan, zoom and the right-click export menu; image export comes free from pyqtgraph, which is why there is no separate data-export command.

nodes.label: Python Launcher ncv()
nodes.rationale: `from ncv import ncv` gives the same entry point as the console script and `python3 -m ncv`, accepting a path or list of paths plus miss and usex arguments mirroring --miss and --xarray.

nodes.label: Qt Designer Forms in ncv/ui
nodes.rationale: main_window.ui, scatter_panel.ui, contour_panel.ui, map_panel.ui, map_unavailable.ui and matrix_panel.ui are loaded at runtime with PyQt6.uic.loadUi; pyqtgraph widgets, dimension selectors and the Matrix model are attached to the loaded forms afterwards, so Designer never needs to know about them.
nodes.source_location: Editing the interface with Qt Designer

nodes.label: Scatter/Line Tab
nodes.rationale: Y and Y2 get fully independent axes, limits and styling so two series on different scales share one X axis; X is optional and falls back to the sample index.

nodes.label: Shared Session and New Window
nodes.rationale: New Window opens another viewer backed by the same session so several views of one dataset stay in sync; opening a file in any of those windows refreshes every window sharing the session.

nodes.label: Matrix Table Formatting and Flipping
nodes.rationale: Cell values and coordinate headers carry independent fixed-point/scientific formats with 0-8 decimals; flipping top-to-bottom or left-to-right keeps data and headers synchronized, and coordinate-size mismatches fall back to zero-based source indices rather than misaligning.

nodes.label: Shared Time Navigation Controls
nodes.rationale: Map and Matrix share one time-navigation widget set active only when the selected variable carries the detected time dimension; slider, dimension selector, displayed frame and Time: label stay synchronized, and boundary mode (once/repeat/reflect) decides animation behavior at the ends.

nodes.label: xarray Reading Path
nodes.rationale: Selected with -x/--xarray; uses xarray.open_dataset for one file and open_mfdataset for many. Without xarray installed the netCDF4 reader remains and the Open xarray button is simply hidden rather than erroring.

nodes.label: Testing Expectations
nodes.rationale: Tests pin the architectural invariants themselves: import without Cartopy, absence of Tk/CustomTkinter/matplotlib imports, NcvSession.open() on generated files, offscreen window creation, every ncv/ui/*.ui form loading, and the Map tab present-but-informational without Cartopy.

nodes.label: ncv NetCDF Viewer
nodes.rationale: A PyQt6 desktop viewer combining dimension selection, pyqtgraph plots, an optional Cartopy map view, and an array/metadata table in one application; explicitly a viewer, not an editor or export tool.

nodes.label: Forbidden GUI/Plotting Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Package imports must not depend on Tk, CustomTkinter, matplotlib, or Cartopy, keeping the import graph to PyQt6 + pyqtgraph so startup stays light and the optional extras stay genuinely optional.

nodes.label: Optional Cartopy Graceful Degradation
nodes.rationale: Cartopy is optional: a missing install must not break package import or app startup, so the Map tab degrades to an informational/disabled state. Only cartopy.crs and cartopy.feature are used (projection maths and Natural Earth geometry) because neither pulls in matplotlib; all rendering stays pyqtgraph.

nodes.label: Optional xarray Backend Policy
nodes.rationale: xarray is optional; the --xarray path fails with a clear runtime message only when explicitly requested and unavailable, so the default netCDF4 path never pays for an absent dependency.

nodes.label: Runtime .ui Loading with uic.loadUi
nodes.rationale: Qt Designer forms in ncv/ui/*.ui are loaded at runtime rather than compiled to Python, eliminating a generated-code step: editing a form and restarting the app is the whole edit loop, and no generated file can drift from its .ui source.

nodes.label: Single Public Launcher Name
nodes.rationale: `ncv` is the only public launcher name; no `ncvue` compatibility command or function is to be added, avoiding a second name to document, test, and keep working.

nodes.label: Toolkit-Neutral Helper Layer
nodes.rationale: NetCDF, session, and slicing logic is kept free of Qt so Qt widgets consume plain specs and values; this keeps the data layer testable without a GUI and swappable behind any toolkit.

nodes.label: Full-Variable Range Calculation (all)
nodes.rationale: Initial color/value ranges may be computed from a sample of a large variable; the `all` option forces inspection of the complete variable. It is opt-in because full-variable range calculations are expensive for very large arrays.

nodes.label: Group and Multi-File Naming Conflict Rejection
nodes.norm_label: group and multi-file naming conflict rejection
nodes.rationale: Opening multiple files when one contains NetCDF groups is rejected with a clear error because group names and multi-file identifiers are two naming schemes that would be ambiguous if combined in the variable list.

nodes.label: Map Grid Downsampling and Full Res
nodes.norm_label: map grid downsampling and full res
nodes.rationale: Large grids are downsampled by default to keep the map responsive, with `full res` as the explicit opt-in to draw every cell: interactivity is the default, fidelity the deliberate choice.

nodes.label: Widget Object Name Contract
nodes.rationale: Because forms are loaded at runtime, widget object names are the only contract between the .ui files and their Python controllers; renaming or removing an object requires updating its Python references and tests in the same change or it fails only at runtime.
